solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Country of fairy stories? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary means the opposite way round, so the extracted letters are read right to left
the run is taken out of the words fairy stories, the letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A question about some land that exists only in fairy tales, then a reversal of the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' takes AIRYS from fAIRY Stories, and 'On the contrary' turns it round. The question mark hints that the suggested fairyland is the very opposite of a real country.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a Middle Eastern nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Cast drinking bitter, and staggering!

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so the throw swallows the sour word

parts.note: to cast is to throw, to sling
tart means sour or bitter in taste

explanation.surface: A drunk actor full of bitter beer reels about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a troupe of actors and 'bitter' like beer, but they are a verb for throw and an adjective for sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means astonishing, which is the figurative sense of staggering.

clue.text: Page clergyman right away

indicators.note: away says the abbreviation for right is taken out of the cleric's title

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A summons for the vicar to come right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Page' looks like a verb for summoning; it is the noun, a sheet of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A recto is the right-hand page of an open book, so it is an example of a page.

clue.text: A rugby forward's very large, by the way

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
OS stands for outsize, very large as a clothing size

explanation.surface: Remarking in passing that a front-row player is huge.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing-size label for very large garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos, used as an aside, means incidentally, the same as by the way.

clue.text: Ring us following shake of great significance

indicators.note: following says the ring and us come after the shake in the answer

parts.note: a shake, as in 'in two shakes', is a moment
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be phoned after a shake-up of some importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something momentous is weighty and far-reaching, a synonym for being of great significance.

clue.text: Thin, a group's leader plunging into lake

indicators.note: plunging into means going inside, so the pieces are put in the lake word

parts.note: a mere is a lake, especially in poetry or English place names

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word group's

explanation.surface: A skinny figure, the head of a party, diving into a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or lean, a synonym for thin.

clue.text: Service small cars before test

indicators.note: before says the cars come first in the answer

parts.note: Minis are small British cars
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: Getting small cars serviced before their MOT test.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a classic small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: A ministry is a government department, which is also called a service in the sense of public service.

clue.text: Loose thing that is put on

definitions.text: Loose thing that is put on

indicators.note: loose suggests letters set free to move, so the word thing is rearranged

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A loose garment that is pulled on.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes the garment itself: a loose thing that is put on, so the definition overlaps the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a loose nightdress that a person puts on for bed.

clue.text: Collection made by Conservative supporting bid

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed beneath, so the party member comes after the bid

parts.note: a bid is an offer
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Money raised by a Conservative backing a bid.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts one piece below another.
explanation.definitionFit: An offertory is the collection of money taken during a church service.

clue.text: Part of play watched in the auditorium

indicators.note: in the auditorium means as heard by an audience, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: watched means seen

explanation.surface: A section of a drama being observed by the theatre audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a subdivision of an act in a play.

clue.text: Find out when? Sure

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone asks when they will learn the truth and is told it is certain.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to establish or discover a fact, synonymous with finding it out.

clue.text: Blunder made by foreman? Almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a gaffer is British slang for a foreman or boss

explanation.surface: A mistake made by the man in charge of the works, or nearly so.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFFER is British slang for a foreman or works boss; 'Almost' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social slip or embarrassing error, a synonym for blunder.

clue.text: Bring information back about old soldier

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes around the abbreviation for old
back says the word for bringing information is read in reverse

parts.note: to bring information is to report it

explanation.surface: Someone asks for news to be brought back concerning a veteran soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REPORT into TROPER, and 'about' wraps it around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier in a cavalry or armoured regiment.

clue.text: Let out group without charge

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A party of people released without being charged with an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free is to release, a synonym for let out as a past tense or participle.

clue.text: I name patient, as a precaution

parts.note: a doctor speaks of a patient as a case

explanation.surface: A doctor gives the name of a patient as a safety measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something just in case means doing it to guard against a possibility, a precaution.

clue.text: Cheese — a part brought into court

indicators.note: brought into means placed inside, so the court abbreviation holds the rest

parts.note: a member is a part, as a limb of the body

explanation.surface: A cheese, or a share of it, carried into a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft French cheese from Normandy.

clue.text: Horrible urge to change one or other

indicators.note: to change says the letters of the word urge are rearranged

parts.note: some can mean an unspecified one, as in 'some person or other'

explanation.surface: An awful impulse to swap one thing for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one or other' looks like a choice between two things, but it stands for an unspecified someone, as in 'some fool or other'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means grisly and repellent, a synonym for horrible.

clue.text: Hint given to a learner? That's natural

parts.note: an element can mean a trace or hint, as in an element of truth
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A tip passed to a beginner, described as only to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means relating to the forces of nature, so natural or primal.

clue.text: Scratch game

definitions.meaning: to scratch or scrape about with the hands, as in scrabbling for a foothold
a board game in which players build words with lettered tiles

explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is both a verb for scraping with the fingers and the trademarked word game.

clue.text: Cheap joke on Russian plane backfired

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the joke follows the reversed plane
backfired suggests something going backwards, so the plane's name is reversed

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian military jet
a crack is a wisecrack, a joke

explanation.surface: A tasteless joke about a Russian aircraft fell flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfired' turns MIG into GIM, and CRACK is placed on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimcrack describes something showy but shoddy, so cheap in the sense of poorly made.

clue.text: All are getting drunk imbibing English beer

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the rearranged letters take in the next piece
getting drunk suggests confusion, so the letters of all are are rearranged

explanation.surface: Everyone gets drunk on traditional English beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting drunk' rearranges ALL ARE into REALAL, and 'imbibing' takes E inside it. Real ale is cask-conditioned British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is cask beer brewed and served by traditional methods, so it is a type of beer.

clue.text: Eryngo growing wild, wild on grey breakwater

indicators.note: growing wild suggests disorder, so the letters of the plant name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sea holly running wild on a grey stone sea wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue holds a second anagram too: 'on grey', marked 'wild', also gives the answer. Eryngo is sea holly, a seaside plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A groyne is a low wall built out into the sea to check erosion, a kind of breakwater.

clue.text: Runs slip away causing setback to recovery

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
time is said to elapse when it slips away

explanation.surface: A cricketer's runs drying up as a comeback falters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' suggests a cricket fielding position next to 'Runs', but it means pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a return of illness after improvement, so a setback to recovery.

clue.text: Stadium beginning to get full

indicators.note: beginning to means just the first letter of get

parts.note: round can mean full or plump, as in a round figure

explanation.surface: A sports arena starting to fill up.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground is a sports field with its stands, as in a football ground, a stadium.

clue.text: Buddhist priest describing naughty dance

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing around, so the priest surrounds the naughty word

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or priest
bad means naughty, of a child

explanation.surface: A Buddhist cleric talking about a risqué dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian partner dance, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Off the booze during card game and bingo

indicators.note: during means within, so the teetotal letters sit inside the card game

parts.note: loo is an old card game
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: Staying sober while playing cards and bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance with numbered cards, much like bingo.

clue.text: Issue over tenancy agreement

parts.note: re means concerning, about, which over can also mean
a lease is a contract letting property to a tenant

explanation.surface: A dispute arising over a rental contract.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a record or film is to issue it, so the two are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Sign of tooth decay, canine's first to be extracted

indicators.note: to be extracted means taken out, so the letter is removed from the decay word

parts.note: caries is the medical term for tooth decay

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of canine's

explanation.surface: Signs of a rotten tooth, with the canine due to be pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries is the first sign of the zodiac, the Ram.

clue.text: Letter from Greece among post he takes

indicators.note: among says the letters sit within the words post he takes

explanation.surface: A letter sent from Greece in the mail that he collects.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Down measure of beer when framing introduction to rather an original plan

parts.note: down means sad or depressed, which is feeling blue

indicators.note: when framing says the beer measure goes around the next piece

parts.note: a pint is a standard measure for beer

indicators.note: introduction to means only the opening letter of rather is used

explanation.surface: Feeling low over a pint, a drinker sketches out an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a technical drawing or a model design, an original plan for later work.

clue.text: Recovering, continuously swallowing them

indicators.note: swallowing means the phrase takes the next word inside itself

parts.note: on end means without a break, as in 'for hours on end'

explanation.surface: A patient keeps on gulping down the pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the mend is an idiom for getting better after illness, so recovering.

clue.text: Stand in calm lake

parts.note: ease is a calm, relaxed state
L is a standard abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: Wading into a tranquil lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame that holds a painting, a kind of stand.
